page: The Amazon Web Services r8gd.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs operating across 2 physical cores at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, paired with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio that characterizes AWS memory-focused profiles. The instance includes a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Hardware-accelerated graphics are omitted with a zero GPU count.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced single-threaded efficiency alongside capacity constraints typical of a dual-core footprint. Single-core performance achieves middle-tier results, indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1707.1 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1815.0. Data processing throughput shows distinct peaks, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression operating at a strong 14.16 GB/sec. Conversely, overall aggregate throughput is constrained by core count; multi-core stress-ng registers at 3402.08, while multi-core Geekbench reaches 3223.0. Memory throughput reaches 56.37 GB/sec for uncached read-only large blocks, aligning with mid-range operational capabilities.

The hardware configuration provides high memory density and high-speed local NVMe scratch storage at entry-level core counts. While compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks, ray tracing, and large language model inference are hindered by the modest two-core layout, the instance maintains steady performance for memory-bound tasks. The r8gd.large is appropriate for lightweight in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, local caching pipelines, distributed database replica nodes, and microservice workloads requiring high memory allocation per thread alongside fast ephemeral disk access.
description: The Amazon Web Services r8gd.large is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual machine powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It is configured with 2 dedicated 2.8 GHz vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a dedicated 118 GB NVMe SSD instance storage volume, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Delivering an 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio, this instance is structured for memory-intensive applications requiring localized high-speed disk operations. Benchmark evaluation reveals steady single-core computing efficiency, with a Geekbench single-core rating of 1815.0 and PassMark database operations scoring 3033.95. However, multi-core throughput remains restricted by the physical two-core ceiling. The r8gd.large is suited for operational scenarios such as Redis caching, small transactional databases, memory-backed queuing systems, and ephemeral processing pipelines.
